name: favourite-highlight-clears-on-tab-close
description:
A favourite tile kept its selected highlight after the tab it opened was closed. The producer was cleared of it: the Rust core answers `selected:false` for every tile in both states a close can leave (empty strip, and another tab active), and the C++ overlay marks them false whenever it runs. So the open question is not what the model says but whether the surface ever redraws from it, and this scenario is built to tell those two apart rather than to watch a pixel.

Three readings, in order. The run log must carry a close; a fresh model must be BUILT after that close (vlog_after, not mere presence - the same line is logged on every push since launch); and the page must have APPLIED a push, which no log line can show, so apply() bumps window.__atriumApplyCount and the counter is zeroed just before the chord.

The second phase is the discriminating one. installSidebar parks a push in `pending` while a drag is in flight, and the latch clears only on a dragend or drop that still reaches the root. A dragstart with no drop leaves it armed, and from then on every push parks - a sidebar frozen on its last frame, which looks exactly like a tile that will not let go. Phase one uses a synthetic click, which arms nothing; phase two arms the latch by hand first. If phase one is green and phase two hangs on applied-after-drag, the latch is the fault and the model never was.

assertions.desc: Cmd+W took. BrowserController::RemoveTab logs this for a genuine delete only, so a move-out or a teardown cannot stand in for it. Without it a chord that never reached the window leaves the tile lit for an honest reason.

assertions.desc: Ordering, not presence: this line is logged on every push since launch, so its mere existence says nothing about the close. What matters is that the producer ran AGAIN afterwards - which is what makes a stale tile the surface's fault rather than the model's.
and the surface applied that push instead of parking it in `pending`
THE assertion: the closed tab's tile is no longer highlighted, and the grid still has all three.
the second control: phase two starts from a lit tile too

the drag latch had a source to arm from. 'no-source' means the sidebar drew no row and the phase proved nothing. Quoted because this one is a plain eval, which stores the JSON as it comes back - the eval_until reads below store theirs already unwrapped.
THE DISCRIMINATOR: a push still redraws with a drag left armed. A failure here names the latch, and clears the snapshot producer entirely.
